person_note: The Henry-family story and authorial historical transitions are controlled by third-person narration, as the diagnostic event quotes show. The novel also makes World Empire Lost a substantial recurring strand: nine named chapters present von Roon’s participating first-person military memoir, beginning with Victor Henry’s first-person Translator’s Foreword and punctuated by his notes. Because these are sustained, chapter-length sections rather than isolated speech, letters, or quotations, the methodology’s rule for sustained sections in different persons yields ALTERNATING. The quote sample happens not to include an explicit narratorial I/we from those chapters, but the complete text and independent structural analysis establish them. The only interpretive uncertainty is whether to subordinate the fictional treatise as an embedded document; its repeated chapter-level placement makes it constitutive enough to satisfy the alternating-person rule.
